note: Ground-truth adjudications under the SFIP Dwelling Form (Oct 2021 edition, 44 CFR Part 61 App A(1)). Section references are to that form. All figures USD.

components.calc: Replacement-cost settlement applies (principal residence; limit >= 80% RCV and = NFIP max) [VII.R.1.a, R.2]. Least of: limit 250,000; repair cost of damaged part 48,200; amount actually spent 48,200 => 48,200. Less building deductible 2,000 [VI.A] => 46,200. Repairs completed, so R.2.c holdback condition satisfied.
RCV settlement: 30,000 - 2,000 building deductible = 28,000.
Contents settle at ACV [VII.R.4.e]: 12,500 - 2,000 contents deductible = 10,500. Separate deductibles per VI.B.
Loss 1,400 does not exceed the 2,000 building deductible [VI.A] => nothing payable.

RCV settlement: repair cost 310,000 - deductible 2,000 = 308,000, but payment cannot exceed the least amount in R.2.a, which includes the Coverage A limit of liability 250,000 [VII.R.2.a.(1)] => 250,000.
Jewelry class capped at 2,500 for any one loss [III.B.8.c]: min(9,000, 2,500) = 2,500. Ordinary contents ACV 3,000. Subtotal 5,500 - contents deductible 2,000 [VI.A, VI.B] = 3,500.
Sewer backup is excluded unless there is a flood in the area and the flood is the proximate cause of the backup [V.D.5]. No flood existed => excluded. Also fails II.B flood definition.
RCV settlement: 148,000 - 2,000 deductible = 146,000.

Substantial damage (repair cost 60% >= 50% of market value) with enforced ordinance => eligible [III.D.3.a.(2)]. Elevation cost 42,000 capped at Coverage D limit 30,000 [III.D.2]. No deductible applies to Coverage D [VI.C.3]. Combined A + D = 176,000 <= statutory max 250,000 [III.D.2].

Sandbags/supplies/pump expenses eligible: evacuation order issued and flooding occurred nearby [III.C.2.a.(2)]. Capped at 1,000 [III.C.2.a.(1)]; deductible does not apply [VI.C.1]. min(1,350, 1,000) = 1,000.
Not principal residence => ACV settlement [VII.R.4.i]. ACV = repair cost 62,000 - depreciation 11,000 = 51,000 [II.C.2]. Less building deductible 5,000 => 46,000.
No Coverage B purchased (contents limit 0) [III.B.1]; additionally the property belongs to the tenant, not the named insured or household family members [III.B.1.a].
No inundation of normally dry land => no flood [II.B.1]. Wind/windstorm excluded [V.D.8]; rain and water spray excluded [V.D.3].
Covered dwelling damage ACV 9,000 - 5,000 deductible = 4,000.
Fence [IV.12], driveway/exterior surfaces [IV.9], and pool equipment [IV.14] are Property Not Insured => 0.

Underinsured dwelling => pay the GREATER of (1) ACV of damaged part or (2) proportion of repair cost, capped at limit [VII.R.4.a]. Proportion = 120,000 / (80% x 200,000 RCV = 160,000) = 0.75; 0.75 x 40,000 = 30,000, after deductible 1,000 => 29,000. ACV route: 32,000 - 1,000 deductible [VI.A] => 31,000. Greater => 31,000.

In a basement, building coverage is limited to the III.A.8.a list: furnace 4,500 + water heater 1,200 = 5,700 covered; finished (taped/painted) drywall, carpet and finishes NOT covered (only unfinished, untaped drywall qualifies [III.A.8.a.(3)]). 5,700 - 1,000 building deductible = 4,700.

In a basement, contents coverage is limited to the III.B.5 list: washer/dryer 1,800 + food freezer and food 900 = 2,700 covered; basement furniture NOT covered. 2,700 - 1,000 contents deductible = 1,700.

Detached garage covered up to 10% of dwelling limit: 10% x 120,000 = 12,000 [III.A.3]; use reduces the building limit. Garages settle at ACV [VII.R.4.d]: min(15,000, 12,000) = 12,000 - 1,000 building deductible = 11,000.
Antiques paid at functional value only [III.B.9]: 1,500 (not 8,000). Plus ordinary contents ACV 2,500. Subtotal 4,000 - 1,000 contents deductible = 3,000.
Inundation covered less than two acres and only one property => does not meet the definition of flood [II.B.1]. No covered peril.
